{
  "candidate_rtl": "module addr_calcu(
    input [7:0] address,
    input [7:0] ptr1, ptr2,
    input [7:0] b,
    input control,
    output [15:0] count
);
    parameter [7:0] base = 8'b10000000;

    wire [7:0] ab_p, ab_g;
    wire [15:0] count1, count2;

    assign ab_p = address ^ b;
    assign ab_g = address & b;

    addr_calcu_branch #(.BASE(base)) branch1 (
        .ab_p(ab_p), .ab_g(ab_g), .ptr(ptr1), .result(count1)
    );
    addr_calcu_branch #(.BASE(base)) branch2 (
        .ab_p(ab_p), .ab_g(ab_g), .ptr(ptr2), .result(count2)
    );

    assign count = (control == 1'b1) ? count1 : count2;
endmodule

module addr_calcu_branch(ab_p, ab_g, ptr, result);
    parameter [7:0] BASE = 8'b10000000;
    input [7:0] ab_p, ab_g;
    input [7:0] ptr;
    output [15:0] result;

    wire [7:0] residue;
    wire subtract_page;
    wire [7:0] s, m;
    wire [7:0] p, g;
    wire [8:0] c;
    wire [7:0] low_sum;
    wire bit8, negative;

    // The assignment deliberately retains only the low eight bits.
    // With BASE=128 this becomes an inversion of ptr[7].
    assign residue = ptr - BASE;
    assign subtract_page = |residue;

    // Carry-save representation of address + b + residue.
    assign s = ab_p ^ residue;
    assign m = ab_g | (ab_p & residue);

    // Add s and (m << 1), with explicit grouped carry lookahead.
    assign p = s ^ {m[6:0], 1'b0};
    assign g = s & {m[6:0], 1'b0};
    assign c[0] = 1'b0;
    assign c[1] = 1'b0;
    assign c[2] = g[1];
    assign c[3] = g[2] | (p[2] & g[1]);
    assign c[4] = g[3] | (p[3] & g[2])
                         | (p[3] & p[2] & g[1]);
    assign c[5] = g[4] | (p[4] & c[4]);
    assign c[6] = g[5] | (p[5] & g[4])
                         | (p[5] & p[4] & c[4]);
    assign c[7] = g[6] | (p[6] & g[5])
                         | (p[6] & p[5] & g[4])
                         | (p[6] & p[5] & p[4] & c[4]);
    assign c[8] = g[7] | (p[7] & g[6])
                         | (p[7] & p[6] & g[5])
                         | (p[7] & p[6] & p[5] & g[4])
                         | (p[7] & p[6] & p[5] & p[4] & c[4]);

    assign low_sum = p ^ c[7:0];
    assign bit8 = m[7] ^ c[8] ^ subtract_page;
    assign negative = subtract_page & ~m[7] & ~c[8];
    assign result = {{7{negative}}, bit8, low_sum};
endmodule
",
  "bottleneck": "The supplied critical path starts at control and passes through substantial arithmetic logic before reaching the replicated upper output bits. The rewrite keeps control exclusively in the final result selection and replaces cascaded subtraction/addition with carry-save compression followed by an eight-bit grouped-lookahead addition.",
  "rewrite": "For each branch, define residue=(ptr-base) modulo 256. Then -((base-ptr) modulo 256)=residue-256*(residue!=0). Compute address+b+residue using shared address/b propagate and generate signals, branch-local carry-save compression, and explicit carry lookahead. Apply the remaining 256 correction directly to bit 8 and the replicated upper bits. At base=128, residue generation requires only inversion of the pointer's most significant bit.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "Expected to shorten the control path to final selection and reduce arithmetic depth on data paths relative to the 2.38 ns baseline. No mapped timing result is available; the actual maximum arrival and gain require the specified synthesis and STA flow.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Duplicates the branch-local compressor and carry-lookahead network to preserve late selection, while sharing address/b preprocessing and eliminating full-width arithmetic. Area is expected to be competitive with the baseline, but compliance with the 1311.632960 um^2 cap and zero electrical violations must be established by mapping and electrical checks.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Preserves the module interface, unsigned widths, eight-bit base parameter, modulo-256 offset behavior, modulo-65536 final arithmetic, and control selection for every two-state input. The mathematical result lies between -255 and 510, allowing bits 15:9 to be represented by a replicated negative indicator. The identity also holds for other eight-bit base values. No storage, clocks, latency, input assumptions, or external dependencies are introduced. Mapped equivalence has not been run."
}
